evidence: Cic. Sen. 24: tam senex quī sē annum nōn putet posse vīvere
terms.comment: Ages: quārtum agō annum et octōgēsimum, I am in my eighty-fourth year (Cic. Sen. 32); see how old are you.

evidence: Cic. Red. Sen. 9 (M-O s.v. last year)

terms.gloss: next year; in a story, the following year
evidence: Traupman 89: the following year, proximus annus
terms.comment: proximus looks either way; see last (the one before this).

phrases.latin: nēmō enim est tam senex quī sē annum nōn putet posse vīvere
phrases.english: for no one is so old that he doesn’t think he can live another year
you will have grape juice all year
I am in my eighty-fourth year

sources: Lewis & Short: annus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. last year.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 89, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
